001.steps:
1) Intiate SSH to device: ssh ip_address
 2) Verify that cannot connect
001.initial: Device setup with IP but with ssh disabled on the port.
001.title: Connection to port with SSH disabled
001.result: Should not be able to connect when SSH disabled.

010.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 2) Wait for connection.
 3) Repeat steps 1-2 creating additional sessions until the maximum(4) is reached.
 4) Initiate a aditional SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 5) Verify that this is rejected.
010.title: Multiple SSH sessions attempts

011.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr and go to config level.
 2) Wait for connection.
 3) Initiate web management session with browser choose to not preempt.
 4) Verify that all sessions are functioning properly by entering commands.
 5) Go to config level.
 6) Verify configuration in GUI while SSH active.
011.title: Web session with SSH

012.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 2) Wait for connection.
 3) Go to the configuration level: configure
 4) Intiate another SSH session.
 5) Attempt to go to the configuration level: configure
 6) Verify preempt message.
 7) Choose OK
 8) Verify that the other session is put at top level and that this session enters configuration level.
012.title: Config Session Lock SSH
012.result: Only one config level session can be present at the same time.

013.steps:
1) In Serial Console go to configuration level:configure
 2) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 3) Wait for connection.
 4) Attempt to go to the configuration level in SSH session: configure
 6) Verify preempt message.
 7) Choose OK
 8) Verify that the other session is put at top level and that this session enters configuration level.
013.title: Config Session Lock Serial Console
013.result: Only one config level session can be present at the same time.

034.steps:
Monitor system resources during test to verify that there are no memory leaks.
 1) Initiate SSH to device:
 ssh ip_addr
 2) Wait for connection
 3) Go to configuration level.
 4) Paste a large configuration into the SSH window.
 5) Wait until the commands finish.
 6) Verify that the running configuration has been changed appropriately.
034.title: Pasting Commands
034.result: Paste should happen with no memory leaks or other problems.  Performance should not be greatly effected.

035.steps:
1)Set administrative timeout to 1
 2)On serial console do "diag show processes" continuous
 3)Connect ssh session.
 4)Do "diag show processes" continuous
 5))Allow timeout to occur.
 6)SSH session should be disconnected.
 7)Reconnect with an SSH session.
 9)Do several shows.
 10)Verify no extra data is displayed.
035.title: Verify PTY Cleanup
035.result: PTY buffer is cleaned up after sessions

036.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 2) Wait for connection.
 3) From GUI disable ssh connection
 4) From serial console verify ssh session has been removed with "diag show processes" (There should be a tSshC process for each ssh session or not if disconnected)
 5) Verify ssh session is still there.
 6) From SSH session enter some commands.
 7) Verify disconnect
 8) Initiate SSH to device: ssh
 9) Verify that cannot connect.
036.title: Disable SSH using GUI with connection
036.result: Disabling remove current session and prevents future connections.   Disabling does not cause any problems.

037.steps:

037.title: Putty with miscomputed encryption key
037.result: Device should recover from this without problems.

038.steps:
1) From Serial Console set timeout to 1
 2) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_address
 3) Wait for connection.
 4) Type configure
 5) Wait for the timeout
 5) From serial console verify ssh session has been removed with "diag show processes" (There should be a tSshC process for each ssh session or not if disconnected)
 6) Try to go to config level from CLI
 7) Verify success.
038.title: Timeout of SSH session that is at config level.
038.result: Timeout of ssh session at config level clears the session and allows other session to go to config level.

004.steps:
1) Set SSH port on System > Administration page to 54022
 2) Initiate SSH to device on port 22: ssh ip_address
 2) Verify cannot connect
 3) Initiate SSH to device on new port : ssh ip_address -p 54022
 4) Verify can connect
 5) Reset port to default using GUI.
 6) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_address -p 54022
 7) Verify cannot connect
 8) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_address
 9) Verify can connect
004.initial: Device setup with SSH enabled.\n\nSsh port assigned to non-standard such as 54022.
004.title: Connection on non-standard TCP port
004.result: Refusal of  SSH connection on previously assigned ports  and successful connection on assigned port.

046.steps:
1. Enable SSH Management on X0 port. 
 2. Create a Address Object range of addresses in X0 subnet,
 
 3, In SSL-VPN Client settings default device profile set this address on the Settings tab and add X0 subnet in Client Routes, 
 
 4. In SSL-VPN Server enable SSLVPN access on WAN and LAN.
 
 5. Enable SSH Management over SSL-VPN on SSL-VPN server page.
 
 6.  Create access rule SSLVPN > LAN to allow SSH access to X0 IP. 
 7. Create user that is member of SSL-VPN services and Sonicwall administrators, 
 also allow VPN access to  user to X0 IP. 
 8. Make a NetExtender connection to X1 and log in as user.
 9. Make SSH connection over SSL-VPN.

046.title: Connection through SSL-VPN with SSH management enabled

006.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 2) Wait for connection.
 3) From Serial Console at Configure > Interface level: no management ssh.
 4) Verify ssh session has been removed with "diag show processes" (There should be a tSshC process for each ssh session or not if disconnected)
 6) From SSH session verify disconnect.
 7) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 8) Verify that cannot connect.
006.title: Disable SSH using Serial with connection
006.result: Disabling remove current session and prevents future connections.

007.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 2) Wait for connection.
 3) Login.
 4) Type configure
 5) Edit the interface and shows "no management ssh" and commit. - SSH session is disconnected
 6) From serial console verify ssh session has been removed with "diag show processes" (There should be a tSshC process for each ssh session or not if disconnected)
 7) Attempt SSH connection to device: ssh ip_addr
007.title: Disable SSH using SSH
007.result: Disabling disconnects user and removes SSH session.  Subsequent connections are not allowed.

008.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_addr
 2) Wait for connection.
 3) Change the IP of the device:
 >configure
 >interface X0
 >ip-assignment LAN static
 >ip address new_ip
 >exit
 >commit
 4) From Serial Console type show sessions
 5)  From serial console verify ssh session has been removed with "diag show processes" (There should be a tSshC process for each ssh session or not if disconnected)
 6) Initiate SSH to device: ssh new_ip
 7) Verify that can connect.
008.title: Change IP using SSH
008.result: Changing IP disconnects current session.  Changing IP now allows connection at new IP.

009.steps:
1) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_address.
 2) Change the SSH port of the device from configuration > administration: ssh port 54022 - user is disconnected.
 3) Initiate SSH to device on port 22: ssh ip_address
 4) Verify cannot connect
 5) Initiate SSH to device on new port : ssh ip_address -p 54022
 6) Verify can connect
 7) Change the SSH port of the device to default: ssh port 22 - user is disconnected
 8) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_address -p 54022
 9) Verify cannot connect
 10) Initiate SSH to device: ssh ip_address
 11) Verify can connect
009.title: Change SSH port using SSH
009.result: User cannot connect on previous port but can on port that was changed to.
